source: NCERT Class VI, Exploring Society: India and Beyond, Social/Political Life Ch. 3 (Grassroots Democracy – Part 2: Rural Areas).

sections.heading: 1. Panchayati Raj — Rural Local Government
points: **Panchayati Raj** = the system of **local self-government in rural (village) areas**.
Given **constitutional status** by the **73rd Constitutional Amendment (1992)**.

sections.heading: 2. Gram Sabha — The Foundation
points: The **Gram Sabha** is the assembly of **all adult voters** of a village (panchayat area).
It is the **base of the whole system** — it discusses village needs, approves plans and budgets, and holds the Gram Panchayat **accountable**.
It meets a few times a year; every voter can take part **directly** (direct democracy at the grassroots).

sections.heading: 3. Gram Panchayat — Structure
points: The **Gram Panchayat** is the **elected executive** of the village, chosen by the Gram Sabha.
**Sarpanch (Pradhan)** = the elected **head**.
**Panch (ward members)** = elected members representing wards.
**Panchayat Secretary** = an appointed official who keeps records and helps run it.
Term = **five years**.

sections.heading: 4. Functions of the Gram Panchayat
points: **Basic services:** drinking water, village roads, street lighting, drainage, sanitation.
Maintaining **records** (births, deaths); running local schools/health under schemes.
Helping settle **local disputes** and supporting development works.
Collecting some **local taxes** and using **government grants** for village development.

sections.heading: 5. Elections and Representation
points: Panchayat elections are held every **five years**.
**Reservation** of seats for **Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and women** ensures fair representation (many States reserve **one-third to one-half** of seats for women).
This makes local democracy **inclusive**.

sections.heading: 6. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Panchayati Raj = rural local self-government; 3 tiers: Gram Panchayat (village) → Panchayat Samiti (block) → Zila Parishad (district).
73rd Constitutional Amendment (1992) gave it constitutional status.
Gram Sabha = assembly of all adult voters — the foundation & watchdog.
Head of Gram Panchayat = Sarpanch/Pradhan; members = Panch; official = Secretary.
Term = 5 years; seats reserved for SC/ST and women.

sections.heading: 7. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Gram Sabha** (all voters) is different from **Gram Panchayat** (the elected body) — do not confuse.
Three tiers in order: **Gram Panchayat → Panchayat Samiti → Zila Parishad**.
Constitutional status came from the **73rd** Amendment (rural); the **74th** is for **urban** bodies.
The head of the Gram Panchayat is the **Sarpanch**, not the Secretary (who is an appointed official).
